questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What is the main difference between amphibians and reptiles?
A. Their habitats
B. Whether they must live in water at some point in their life
C. Whether they eat insects or not
Answer: B. Amphibians typically have a life cycle that includes both aquatic and terrestrial stages, while reptiles do not. Additionally, whereas reptiles are born with lungs, amphibians are born with gills and often develop lungs later in life.
questions.de: Reptilien kommen mit Lungen zur Welt; womit atmen die meisten Amphibien, wenn sie als Wasserlarven schlüpfen?
questions.en: Reptiles are born with lungs; what do most amphibians breathe with when they hatch as aquatic larvae?

timeline.labelEn: First major groups of amphibians evolve from lobe-finned fish in the Devonian
timeline.labelDe: Die ersten großen Amphibiengruppen entwickeln sich im Devon aus Fleischflossern

questions.notes: Not universal: some amphibians develop directly without a gilled larval stage. The key reproductive difference is that reptiles lay amniotic (shelled) eggs on land while amphibians need water for their shell-less eggs.

questions.cardText:
[Physics] If you move your hand and your head to get their shadows to overlap under the sun, what will you see right before they overlap?
A. One shadow bulges into the other
B. They become brighter
C. They create a rainbow
Answer: A. This effect is called the shadow blister effect.
questions.de: Wie heißt der Effekt, bei dem sich ein Schatten kurz vor der Berührung mit einem anderen scheinbar zu diesem hin ausbeult?
questions.en: What is the name of the effect in which one shadow seems to bulge toward another just before the two touch?

timeline.labelEn: Ray-theory analysis of the shadow blister effect published in Applied Optics
timeline.labelDe: Strahlenoptische Analyse des Schattenblaseneffekts in Applied Optics veröffentlicht

questions.notes: The effect has no established German name; 'Schattenblaseneffekt' is a literal rendering of 'shadow blister effect'. The timeline uses the 1999 Applied Optics paper cited by Wikipedia; the effect's first description is not dated there.
